evidence: The paper uses ranger's random forest implementation (v.0.11.2) solely for classification accuracy testing: "performance on the combined 16s rRNA gene and ITS testing data showed high accuracy in classifying samples to compartment but not to rootstock (98% and 35% accuracy, respectively)." The authors conclude: "These data corroborate other analyses that point to compartment as the primer determinant of microbiota diversity within a vine." No variable importance measures are reported or interpreted; instead, the paper relies on PERMANOVA (explaining 40.7% of bacterial and 55% of fungal variance), DESeq2 differential abundance analysis, and linear models for substantive conclusions.
